title: Paul Buchheit on AI abundance: sell outcomes, stay agile, build for a 10x-intelligence world
summary: Paul Buchheit talks about a world with 10x to 100x more intelligence, and what it means for health, energy and work. For founders, the useful parts are that AI startups win by selling outcomes with immediate ROI, that agile teams beat fixed plans, and that regulated markets often open after someone just ships.

principles.text: Back smart, agile teams that keep re-evaluating instead of locking into a long-term plan, since the future is hard to predict.
principles.quote: the teams that are really performing are the ones that are continually re-evaluating continually updating you know they don't have like a 5-year plan that they're like locked into

principles.text: Startups beat incumbents on speed because established companies cannot pivot as fast.
principles.quote: more established companies have just like no capacity to to move and pivot as quickly as as the startups can do

principles.text: Sell the service and its result, not the software. Customers get immediate ROI and revenue scales faster with fewer people.
principles.quote: the startups that actually just deliver a service essentially so that their customers get basically immediate Roi right so instead of necessarily like selling them software they sell them you know

principles.text: Pair AI with a human professional so the expert handles several times more customers and the customer gets a better experience.
principles.quote: the doctor is able to see you know four times as many patients and the patient actually gets a much better experience because they get to to spend a long time you know talking through their situation

principles.text: Do not wait for regulation to clear a path. Ship, and the rules often catch up afterwards, as with Uber.
principles.quote: they just went and did it right and then it became legal after they did it

principles.text: Have a clear vision of the destination even if the steps are messy, or you will make the wrong decisions along the way.
principles.quote: if you don't even have a vision of what it is you're trying to do then you're not going to make the right decisions to get yourself there
